children: Energy stocks grabbed the spotlight this week as Wall Street digested a wave of third-quarter earnings, led by major reports from key refiners like Marathon Petroleum
and top oil producers including Devon Energy

While uncertainty around energy prices can influence earnings expectations across the sector, companies trading at discounts to their fundamentals may offer opportunities for investors looking for growth at a reasonable price.
In this week's earnings recap, nine tickers reported results, out of which eight companies exceeded EPS expectations, while one reported in-line. All nine companies topped revenue expectations.
Below are the latest quarterly reports from some of the key players who reported results this week:

reported Q3 non-GAAP EPS of $26.93, beating analyst estimates by $0.93, while revenue surged 57.6% year over year to $56.49 billion, exceeding expectations by $12.68 billion. Marathon Petroleum outlined a $4.2B mid-con divestiture and targets Gulf Coast reinvestment as 4Q throughput is guided at 2.8M bpd.
reported Q3 non-GAAP EPS of $1.42, beating analyst estimates by $0.11, while revenue rose 58.4% year over year to $6.86 billion, exceeding expectations by $10 million.

reported Q3 non-GAAP EPS of $0.54, in line with analyst estimates, while revenue increased 10.3% year over year to $3.22 billion, beating expectations by $290 million. Tracking toward the upper half of 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance range of $8.3 billion to $8.5 billion.

reported Q3 revenue of $5.6 billion, up 34.9% year over year and beating analyst estimates by $830 million, while adjusted EBITDA increased 18% to $1.5 billion. The company raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA outlook to at least $6.0 billion and maintained its 2026 net growth capital expenditure estimate of approximately $5.0 billion.
